name: The Sinking City
description: Follow a radar displacement signal across four illustrative checkpoints. Explore how a persistent trajectory could intersect with low terrain and drainage sensitivity.
limitations: Line-of-sight displacement is not vertical subsidence. Orbit geometry and independent validation are required.
The four values and all spatial footprints are synthetic. No NISAR granule has been ingested.
Rainfall does not directly alter the projected radar displacement in this model.

watchAreas.name: Inland corridor
watchAreas.rationale: Persistent simulated signal; contextual sensitivity is lower.

watchAreas.name: Eastern sector
watchAreas.rationale: Review the next observation for signal persistence.

evidence.label: NISAR GUNW observation contract
evidence.source: NASA–ISRO NISAR GUNW • synthetic fixture
evidence.method: Four manually specified illustrative observations; no satellite scene processed.
evidence.assumption: The example emulates a quality-controlled, co-registered time series.
evidence.limitation: Line-of-sight displacement is not vertical subsidence. Orbit geometry and independent validation are required.
evidence.relationship: Repeated acquisitions allow a temporal trend to be estimated.

evidence.label: Persistent temporal signal
evidence.source: Illustrative GUNW time series
evidence.method: Theil–Sen median pairwise slope; persistence = fraction of consecutive changes with the trend direction.
evidence.assumption: Reference frame and processing are consistent between acquisitions.
evidence.limitation: Four synthetic observations cannot establish a real-world trend or statistically robust acceleration.
evidence.relationship: Context helps interpret which continuation scenarios merit attention.

evidence.relationship: Terrain and system sensitivity condition the relevance of environmental triggers.

evidence.label: Rainfall & antecedent moisture

evidence.method: A user-selected intensity profile across days 1–10. Values represent a sensitivity index, not mm of rainfall.
